title: Pipeline Run Context
description: Manifest for a single pipeline run. See docs/context-json-guide.md. Each review_gates entry is a boolean or an audit-field object (oneOf accepts both, backward-compatible).

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the document conforms to, currently '1.0'.

run_id.description: Unique per-run identifier. Convention: ISO-8601-ish timestamp + short hash, e.g. 2026-05-28T14-32-01Z-a1b2c3d.

id.description: Top of the traceability chain. STORY-XXX for manual mode, the Jira issue key for Jira mode.

path.description: Relative path to the local Markdown copy of the story.

jira_issue_key.description: Required when source == 'jira'. Equal to story.id in that case.

acceptance_criteria.description: One AC per element. The array index is the canonical position used by risks[].related_acs.

risks.description: First traceability anchor after the story. Each entry gets a RISK-XXX id.

severity.description: The risk level. With likelihood and impact it MUST be their matrix cell (enforced below).

likelihood.description: OPTIONAL (risk matrix). How likely the risk is to happen: from the change itself (code_change_context: size, complexity, files touched) and the defect history of the area (npm run defect-history). Given together with impact.

impact.description: OPTIONAL (risk matrix). How much it costs the business or the user when it happens: from the story (money, data, access, a blocked journey). Given together with likelihood.

likelihood_basis.description: OPTIONAL. The evidence behind the likelihood, in one sentence: the change, a past defect (story and bug id), or "no history and no diff" when neither exists. Never invented.

items.description: One risk. Severity is the risk level the rest of the pipeline reads (priorities, coverage, the release rules). When likelihood and impact are given, severity is their cell in the risk matrix (docs/context-json-guide.md): likelihood x impact, low-low/low-medium/medium-low are low; high-high/high-medium/medium-high are high; the rest are medium.

code_change_context.description: OPTIONAL. SECONDARY context only: the diff of a linked PR, used to sharpen regression scope and risk prioritization. It NEVER defines expected behavior — acceptance_criteria remain the source of truth (CLAUDE.md §3.8). Populated by the Analyst (Mode B) only when the Jira story has a linked PR; absent otherwise (the pipeline runs identically with no diff). Filled via the read-only GitHub MCP; no custom diff engine, no deploy/ECR infra.

linked_pr.description: URL of the linked pull request, e.g. https://github.com/org/repo/pull/123.

base_sha.description: The base/target SHA (the 'deployed' side). May be a configured branch like main.

related_risk_ids.description: Optional. RISK-XXX this changed file maps to, linking code change -> risk for regression prioritization.

summary.description: Short LLM summary of what the diff does, in the Analyst's own words. Secondary context, not a requirement.

fetched_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the diff was fetched.

prompt_versions.description: OPTIONAL (prompt versioning). Records which agent prompt VERSION drove this run, keyed by agent name (the frontmatter `name:` of agents/*.md), value = that file's `version:` (semver). This pins a run to the exact prompts that produced it, so a metrics/regression delta can be attributed to a specific prompt change. Absent on older runs (the pipeline runs identically without it). Keys are agent names; this object is NOT a closed enum so new agents can register without a schema change.

additionalProperties.description: Semantic version of the agent prompt used (matches agents/<name>.md frontmatter `version:`).

track.description: OPTIONAL (lite track). How much ceremony this story needs. ABSENT => 'standard' (the four gates; the historical default — documented here, NOT schema-defaulted, so existing files behave unchanged). 'lite' thins ARTIFACTS, never decisions: schema validation, traceability, the automation-decision requirement, and auditable gate records all survive; Gates 1+2 consolidate via review_gates.qa_scope_approved while Gates 3 and 4 stay two distinct recorded decisions. 'full' is everything (highest-risk features); every Red-domain story is held to it. A story may NOT declare 'lite' below its track floor (scripts/track-floor.js); see docs/review-gates.md and docs/pipeline-architecture.md.

track_floor.description: OPTIONAL. The LOWEST track this story is allowed to use, computed by scripts/track-floor.js from the Red-taxonomy domains (docs/healer-guardrails.md §4) plus size heuristics. The runner computes the floor again from story.md and this context, taking the higher, refuses a declared `lite` below it and holds any other track to at least it (a Red-domain story to full). Advisory metadata: absent on older runs and on runs that never considered lite.

reasons.description: Why the floor is what it is (e.g. 'red-domain: Payment flow', '6 acceptance criteria (> 4)'). Empty when the floor is 'lite' (nothing raised it).

artifact_paths.description: Manifest of files this run produces. Empty string means 'not yet produced'.

api_collection.description: OPTIONAL. Path to the story's Postman collection (api-tests/collections/[story-id].postman_collection.json), written by the API Agent for approved automate_api cases. Absent = the conventional path. Reviewed at collection_reviewed (requests) and api_assertions_reviewed (assertions).

api_environment.description: OPTIONAL. Path to the story's Postman environment (api-tests/environments/[story-id].postman_environment.json). Values are read at run time from .env; approvals bind to its keys only, never to secret values.

external_plan.description: OPTIONAL. Path to the external execution plan (planner-input/[story-id].external-plan.json, schemas/external-execution.schema.json) for approved manual, component and skip cases. Reviewed at external_plan_reviewed before any external work.

external_results.description: OPTIONAL. Path to the imported external results (external-evidence/[story-id].results.json), written only by scripts/import-execution.js. Reviewed at external_evidence_reviewed before classification and reporting.

execution_ledger.description: OPTIONAL. Path to analysis/execution-ledger.json, the canonical cross-runner counting model for this run (schemas/execution-ledger.schema.json). ADDITIVE and not required: every context written before it existed stays valid. scripts/normalize-results.js writes the ledger. The existing report-path fields remain for compatibility; they are PATHS, not substitutes for a valid ledger.

review_gates.description: Each gate is a boolean or an optional audit-field object (oneOf); both forms remain valid. The OPTIONAL qa_scope_approved gate consolidates Gates 1 and 2 — see docs/review-gates.md. The four per-gate fields stay required for backward compatibility; qa_scope_approved is additive and never replaces code_reviewed (Gate 4 never consolidates).

qa_scope_approved.description: OPTIONAL. When present and passed, consolidates Gate 1 (requirements_reviewed) and Gate 2 (test_scope_reviewed) into a single approval. The two underlying gates remain present and valid (deprecated, not removed). Same boolean | audit-object shape as the other gates. Gate 4 (code_reviewed) is NEVER consolidated into this.

collection_reviewed.description: OPTIONAL. API Gate 3 (Gate 3'): the human reviewed the collection's requests, variables and endpoint contract for the approved automate_api cases. Required only when the approved scope has API cases. Independent of specs_reviewed; an E2E approval never stands in for it.

external_plan_reviewed.description: OPTIONAL. External Gate 3: the human reviewed the plan for approved manual/component/skip cases — procedures or commands, expected outcomes, evidence required, and the exclusion reasons of skipped cases — before any external work. Required only when the approved scope has such cases.

external_evidence_reviewed.description: OPTIONAL. External Gate 4, always human: the reviewer checked the imported results and their evidence (or, for a skip-only scope, the unexecuted disposition) before classification and reporting. Importing results never sets it; code_reviewed is never set for code that does not exist.

api_assertions_reviewed.description: OPTIONAL. API Gate 4 (Gate 4'): the human reviewed the collection's assertion scripts. Always a human decision, like code_reviewed, and independent of it. Newman runs for the story only while both API approvals are current.

gate_decisions.description: OPTIONAL (continuous improvement). An append-only LOG of gate decision events for this run — both approvals AND rejections. review_gates holds the final state; this holds the history, so metrics can count rejections per run. A rejection is recorded, then a later approval is appended when the human re-approves after rework. Absent on older runs; the pipeline runs identically without it.

gate.description: Which gate. Matches a review_gates key.

opened_at.description: OPTIONAL (gate telemetry). ISO 8601 timestamp of when this gate review STARTED — the moment the gate brief / artifacts were first presented to the reviewer. Enables gate cost in minutes (decided_at - opened_at). Absent on older runs; the pipeline runs identically without it.

notes.description: Why — especially for a rejection (what must change before re-review).

record.description: OPTIONAL. The gate record this decision wrote (scripts/lib/gate-records.js) and the SHA-256 of its text (line endings normalized), taken before it was written. Each record also carries the digest of the record before it, so the trail check (`npm run pipeline -- --history`) reports a missing or edited record, the last one included, and --restore refuses a record or copy that changed. It shows the trail was changed after the fact, not who decided. Absent on decisions recorded before records were chained. Written only by the runner.

finding_dispositions.description: OPTIONAL (Gate 4 only). The reviewer's answer to each Gate 4 static scan finding, given before this decision (scripts/lib/finding-dispositions.js): fixed (the test must change, so the decision is a rejection), wrong (a false alarm), intentional or irrelevant. On a Red-domain story, wrong and intentional carry a reason. A later scan treats a finding answered at the current approval as resolved while the finding is unchanged. Absent on decisions with no scan findings and on older runs. Written only by the runner.

provenance.description: OPTIONAL. What produced each agent step's output (scripts/lib/provenance.js): the SHA-256 of every prompt file the step uses (its agent prompt and skills, or the generated .claude/agents/ definition; null when the file does not exist), the model id and harness version the operator declared (QAIZEN_MODEL, QAIZEN_HARNESS; unknown when undeclared, since the runner cannot see which model ran), the output it describes, and when it was recorded. Recorded the first time the runner sees the output, and again when the output changes. Absent on older runs, which show as unknown; nothing is backfilled. Written only by the runner.

repeat_check.description: OPTIONAL. The repeat check the runner ran before Gate 4 (scripts/lib/repeat-check.js): the generated test run repeat_each times on workers workers, and what happened to each test. input_digest is the Gate 4 input digest it ran against; the record holds only while that digest is current, so a changed test, fixture, config or lock runs it again. outcome flaky stops the run before Gate 4. Absent on runs that reached Gate 4 before the check existed. Written only by the runner.

errors.description: OPTIONAL. The first line of each error Playwright reported for the run as a whole (a file that did not load, a failing global setup), at most five.

execution_identity.description: OPTIONAL. Written only by the runner's execute step: what the Playwright execution was (scripts/lib/execution-identity.js). The report is accepted as this run's evidence only while its digest, its config's digest and the Gate 4 approval digest still match. app_build is QAIZEN_APP_BUILD, or "unknown". No agent writes this.

downgrade_confirmations.description: OPTIONAL. Written only by the runner, after a person confirmed at the terminal (TTY-only) a severity the finalized failure analysis lowered from its rule-based draft: a Red failure lowered, or a failure lowered on a high-severity, Red-domain or untraceable risk. Part of the gate trail, not a fifth gate. Each entry is bound to the analysis bytes it was given for (analysis_sha256), so a later change to the analysis needs a new confirmation. No agent writes this.

healer_attempts.description: OPTIONAL. Written only by scripts/run-healer.js with --apply: one entry per candidate fix submitted for a Green failure (at most three per run, test and original source). The cap is counted from these entries together with the records in analysis/healer-validation/, so deleting the record files does not give an attempt back. Each entry names its record file and that file's SHA-256. Evidence, not an approval: a validated patch still needs human review. No agent writes this.

gate_invalidations.description: OPTIONAL. Approvals the runner returned to pending because what they reviewed changed (or because they predate input binding). Separate from gate_decisions[], which records only HUMAN decisions: an invalidation is not a rejection and never invents one. The prior approval is preserved here and in gate_decisions[].

reviewed_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp, or null when not yet recorded.

opened_at.description: OPTIONAL (gate telemetry). ISO 8601 timestamp of when the review started (gate brief first presented), or null when not recorded. Enables gate cost in minutes (reviewed_at - opened_at).

binding_version.description: OPTIONAL. The binding scheme input_digest was computed under (scripts/lib/approval-binding.js BINDING_VERSION); absent means 1. An approval is always checked against its own scheme's inputs, so approvals recorded before a scheme change keep verifying. Version 2 widens Gate 4 to every file under the Playwright testDir and tests/fixtures, tests/fixtures.ts, their relative-import closure (page objects, helpers), tsconfig.json and package.json. Written only by the runner at a human decision. Version 3 binds Gate 3 to the digests of the Planner's and the Generator's prompt files instead of their declared versions.

input_digest.description: OPTIONAL. SHA-256 over the inputs this gate reviewed, taken at the moment of human approval (scripts/lib/approval-binding.js): Gate 1 = story + interpreted ACs/risks/ambiguities/track; Gate 2 = Gate-1 digest + semantic test cases + planner brief; Gate 3 = Gate-2 digest + spec + the digests of the Planner's and the Generator's prompt files (binding_version 3; before it, their declared prompt_versions); Gate 4 = Gate-3 digest + generated test + the testDir, tests/fixtures and their relative-import closure + Playwright config + tsconfig.json + package.json + dependency lock (binding_version 2; version 1 bound only the generated test, tests/fixtures, the config and the lock); qa_scope_approved = Gate-1 + Gate-2 inputs; collection_reviewed (Gate 3') = Gate-2 digest + collection requests/variables (no assertion scripts) + environment variable names (never values) + endpoint contract; api_assertions_reviewed (Gate 4') = Gate-3' digest + assertion scripts + Newman runner + dependency lock; external_plan_reviewed = Gate-2 digest + external plan; external_evidence_reviewed = external-plan digest + imported results (with evidence digests). When today's inputs no longer match, the approval is stale and the runner returns the gate to pending. An approved gate WITHOUT this field is a legacy approval and needs re-review before the run advances. Written only by the runner at a human decision; never by an agent.

inputs.description: OPTIONAL. The per-input digests behind input_digest (null = the input did not exist), so a stale approval can name exactly which input changed.
